author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: These parsers read HPE Aruba Networking EdgeConnect SD-WAN firewall policy logs, stateful WAN drop logs and appliance audit logs. The data collector receives them over syslog as a remote log receiver set in Orchestrator's Logging template. Firewall policy and WAN drop logs go to Netflow, and audit log lines go to ManagementEvent.
notes:
Setup:
- In Orchestrator, add the data collector as a remote log receiver in the Logging template (UDP, TCP or TCP SSL, minimum severity Notice).
- System, Audit, Firewall and IDS/IPS each need their own facility.

Field mapping:
- Firewall policy logs (netflowd) and stateful WAN drop logs go to Netflow, in the text form or in the JSON form Jsonify sends (Orchestrator 9.4 or later): addresses, ports, application, packet and byte counts, start and end times, source NAT, direction, and allow or deny as flow_action, with the zones, rule tag, overlay, interfaces, VRF, reason and the ClearPass user, device and roles in event_metadata.
- RX and TX counts keep the names ECOS gives them.
- Appliance audit log lines (mgmtd) go to Management Event with the user, address, operation and result.

Time:
- ECOS writes the year after the time in the header (Oct 4 05:17:28 2021 host netflowd[pid]:), so the parser reads the time and the appliance name itself.
- HPE doesn't document the time zone, so the time is read as UTC.

Made up in the samples:
- Samples are made up in the shapes of HPE's appliance logs white paper; the header with the year also follows Splunk Connect for Syslog's Silver Peak test data.

Testing:
- Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (113 of 113 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there.
- Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent (113 of 113 fields).
- No built-in parser claimed these lines in 12 Run Tests.

Known gaps:
- System, alarm, DDoS threshold and IDS/IPS lines aren't claimed.
- HPE notes that ECOS 9.6.4 and 9.7.1 don't export firewall logs for IPv6 flows.
